source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Use last-digit, trailing-zero, and parity patterns to rule out impossible perfect squares.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Perfect square is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Use last-digit, trailing-zero, and parity patterns to rule out' is answered as perfect square rather than units digit.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Perfect square is what produces units digit, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Use last-digit, trailing-zero, and parity patterns to.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is units digit because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Use last-digit, trailing-zero, and parity patterns to rule out' as the operative test.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: units digit is settled by running 'Decide whether a number is a cube or perfect cube and compute simple': A cube number is obtained by multiplying a number by itself three times. Natural-number — on the item about Use last-digit, trailing-zero, and parity patterns to.

intelligence.enrichment: Perfect squares end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9, so a number ending in 2, 3, 7, or 8 is not a perfect square. An allowed last digit does not prove a number is a square, and trailing zeros in a square occur in even counts.
